# 2 Baruch Chapter 17 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** First Fast and Vision

---

**17:1** And-I-answered and-said: "O-LORD, lo! For-thou-dost-announce-to-us the-shortness-of-the-time-that-has-passed and-the-length-of-the-time-to-come.

**17:2** And-thou-hast-shown-us that-it-is-short-and-painful, [this-present-age], but-[as-for] the-future-[age], it-is-long-and-desirable.

**17:3** What-have-we-profited-by-this, seeing-that-we-have-come-into-the-world in-great-suffering, and-that-we-live-only-to-be-saddened-all-our-days?

**17:4** But-you-have-shown-us that-the-adversary has-had-dominion-over-us. But-Adam-first-sinned and-brought-death-upon-all-those-who-were-not-of-his-time."

---

*EMET notes: Baruch's response to the Two-Ages theology. V.4 introduces the Adam-death connection. The theology here is that Adam's sin introduced death but each person bears responsibility for their own sins (elaborated in ch.19).*
